Fix non-terminating unification in verify_chain/3 when certificate issuer DN contains circular cross-references

- The predicate `verify_chain([], _, valid).` at line 12 and `verify_chain([Cert|Rest], TrustStore, Result) :- extract_issuer(Cert, IssuerDN), find_issuer(IssuerDN, TrustStore, IssuerCert), verify_signature(Cert, IssuerCert), verify_chain(Rest, TrustStore, Result).` at line 13 does not include an occurs check, so when a malformed certificate chain contains `issuer(dn([cn('CA-A'), org('MutualTrust')]))` and the trust store contains `cert(subject(dn([cn('CA-A'), org('MutualTrust')])), issuer(dn([cn('CA-B'), org('MutualTrust')])))` alongside `cert(subject(dn([cn('CA-B'), org('MutualTrust')])), issuer(dn([cn('CA-A'), org('MutualTrust')])))`, the `find_issuer/3` predicate enters infinite mutual recursion between CA-A and CA-B because `resolve_issuer_chain/3` at line 47 recursively calls itself via `find_issuer(ParentIssuerDN, Store, ParentCert), resolve_issuer_chain(ParentCert, Store, RootCert)` without maintaining a visited set
- The DCG grammar `san_value(ip(A,B,C,D)) --> [0x87, 0x04], byte(A), byte(B), byte(C), byte(D).` at line 89 for parsing SubjectAltName uses `byte(X) --> [X], { X >= 0, X =< 255 }.` which generates choice points for every possible byte value (0-255) on backtracking — when the DER input is malformed and the first `byte(A)` matches but `byte(B)` fails, Prolog backtracks into `byte(A)` trying all 256 alternatives before failing, then backtracks into the `[0x87, 0x04]` match, causing O(256^4) backtracking for each malformed iPAddress SAN entry
- The `assert_trust_anchor/2` predicate at line 134 uses `assert(trusted(Fingerprint, Cert))` to dynamically add trust anchors to the knowledge base, but `verify_chain/3` calls `retract(trusted(Fingerprint, _))` at line 156 to prevent replay attacks — when two concurrent threads (SWI-Prolog threads via `thread_create/3`) both verify chains that share a common trust anchor, thread A's retract removes the anchor between thread B's `find_issuer` and `verify_signature` calls, causing thread B to fail verification with `existence_error(procedure, trusted/2)` instead of the expected `chain_invalid` error because the predicate itself becomes undefined after the last clause is retracted

- `resolve_issuer_chain/3` maintains a visited list of already-seen issuer DNs: `resolve_issuer_chain(Cert, Store, RootCert) :- resolve_issuer_chain(Cert, Store, [], RootCert).` with `resolve_issuer_chain(Cert, Store, Visited, RootCert) :- extract_issuer(Cert, IDN), \+ member(IDN, Visited), find_issuer(IDN, Store, IC), resolve_issuer_chain(IC, Store, [IDN|Visited], RootCert).`
- Maximum chain depth is enforced with a counter: `verify_chain(Chain, Store, Result) :- length(Chain, Len), Len =< 10, verify_chain_(Chain, Store, Result).` and chains exceeding depth 10 unify Result with `chain_too_deep`
- The DCG `byte/3` rule is replaced with `byte(X) --> [X], { integer(X), between(0, 255, X) }.` using deterministic `between/3` with a cut after successful match: `byte(X) --> [X], { integer(X), X >= 0, X =< 255, ! }.`

- Package body TLS_Validator (tls_validator.adb) declares `type Cert_Chain_Ptr is access all Certificate_Chain_Record'Class;` at line 34 and instantiates `procedure Free_Chain is new Ada.Unchecked_Deallocation(Certificate_Chain_Record'Class, Cert_Chain_Ptr);` at line 37 — the procedure Verify_Peer_Identity calls `Free_Chain(Current_Chain)` at line 189 after validation completes, but the exception handler for Constraint_Error at line 204 also calls `Free_Chain(Current_Chain)` without first checking if Current_Chain is null, causing a double-free when Verify_Certificate_Signature raises Constraint_Error after the chain was already freed during partial validation cleanup at line 178
- The discriminated record `type Certificate_Record(Key_Algorithm : Algorithm_Type := RSA_2048) is record ...` uses a default discriminant, but the variant part at line 67 has `when EC_P256 => Curve_Params : Curve_Parameter_Block(1..32);` and `when EC_P384 => Curve_Params : Curve_Parameter_Block(1..48);` — when a certificate is parsed with Key_Algorithm initially RSA_2048 (default) and later reassigned via `Cert.Key_Algorithm := EC_P384` at line 143 in Parse_SubjectPublicKeyInfo, the variant record's constraint is violated but the Constraint_Error is caught by the outer handler which logs "Parse warning" and continues with the RSA_2048 variant layout, reading 32 bytes of Curve_Params from a record that was allocated with 48-byte P-384 parameters, leaving 16 bytes of uninitialized discriminant-controlled storage
- The generic package `TLS_Cache` instantiated as `package Cert_Cache is new TLS_Cache(Key_Type => Session_ID_Type, Element_Type => Cert_Chain_Ptr, Hash => Session_Hash);` at line 28 stores access values (pointers), and when `Cert_Cache.Evict(Old_Session_ID)` is called by the LRU cleanup task at line 312, it removes the map entry but does not call `Free_Chain` on the stored pointer — the task `Cache_Cleanup_Task` (line 298) runs every 60 seconds with `select or delay 60.0; then abort ...` but the abort causes the cleanup loop to terminate between the `Cert_Cache.Delete` call and the `Free_Chain` call at line 318, leaking the Certificate_Chain_Record on every aborted cleanup cycle

- `Free_Chain` calls are guarded with `if Current_Chain /= null then` and Current_Chain is set to null immediately after each deallocation
- Exception handler at line 204 checks `Current_Chain /= null` before attempting deallocation, preventing double-free
- The discriminated record Certificate_Record is changed to use an immutable discriminant (remove default value) so that discriminant reassignment raises Constraint_Error at the assignment site rather than silently corrupting the variant layout

- The generic TLS_Cache package includes a formal generic parameter `with procedure Finalize_Element(E : in out Element_Type);` that is called by Evict before removing the map entry
- Cache_Cleanup_Task uses `select or delay 60.0;` without `then abort` — the abort-deferred region is replaced with a protected object entry call that ensures atomic delete-then-free semantics
